rules.what: Copies of web pages and images your browser saved so sites load faster.
rules.regrows: Yes. The browser downloads what it needs again as you browse.
rules.safeToDelete: Yes. You stay signed in and keep your history, bookmarks and passwords.

rules.what: Preview frames After Effects saved so playback is faster. Each version keeps its own cache, even after you upgrade.
rules.regrows: Yes. After Effects rebuilds previews as you work, which can take a while on big projects.
rules.safeToDelete: Yes, while After Effects is closed. It's the same as Empty Disk Cache in its settings.

rules.what: Copies of email attachments you opened from Mail. If you edited or signed one after opening it, the changed version may only be here.
rules.regrows: Only when you open those attachments again.
rules.safeToDelete: Usually. Your emails keep the original attachments, but check for files you changed first.

rules.what: Software update files downloaded for an iPhone, iPad or iPod.
rules.regrows: Only if you update a device from this Mac again.
rules.safeToDelete: Yes. Your devices already installed them, or will download them again.

rules.what: Temporary files Xcode creates while building your apps.
rules.regrows: Yes. Xcode rebuilds them the next time you build the project.
rules.safeToDelete: Yes. Your next build just takes a little longer.

rules.what: Simulator copies Xcode makes to run tests in parallel.
rules.regrows: Yes, the next time you run tests in parallel.
rules.safeToDelete: Yes, while Xcode isn't running tests.

rules.what: Saved builds of apps you archived, for example to upload to the App Store.
rules.regrows: No. Only new archives you make appear here.
rules.safeToDelete: Only if you no longer need these builds or their debug symbols for crash reports.

rules.what: Debugging files Xcode copied from a device you connected.
rules.regrows: Yes. Xcode copies them again when you connect a device with that system version.
rules.safeToDelete: Yes. Reconnecting the device brings them back.

rules.what: Simulators and builds Xcode uses to show SwiftUI previews.
rules.regrows: Yes, the next time you open a preview.
rules.safeToDelete: Yes, while Xcode is closed.

rules.what: Cached data the iOS Simulator keeps so it starts faster.
rules.regrows: Yes, as you use the Simulator.
rules.safeToDelete: Yes, while the Simulator is closed.

rules.what: Downloaded copies of code libraries, kept so installs are faster.
rules.regrows: Yes. They download again the next time a project needs them.
rules.safeToDelete: Yes. The next install may be slower and needs an internet connection.

rules.what: Java libraries Maven downloaded for your projects.
rules.regrows: Yes. Maven downloads what a project needs on its next build.
rules.safeToDelete: Usually. Check you don't rely on libraries you installed into it by hand.

rules.what: Shared copies of packages that your pnpm projects link to.
rules.regrows: Yes. pnpm adds packages back when projects need them.
rules.safeToDelete: Not by moving the folder, because projects link into it. Let pnpm clean it instead.

action.guidance: Run “pnpm store prune” in Terminal to remove packages no project uses.

rules.what: Downloaded Python packages Conda keeps to create environments.
rules.regrows: Yes, when you create or update environments.
rules.safeToDelete: Not by moving the folder. Let Conda clean it instead.

rules.what: Test copies of Chrome, Firefox and WebKit downloaded for automated testing.
rules.regrows: Yes. They download again the next time your tests need them.
rules.safeToDelete: Yes. Your tests just download the browsers again.

rules.what: AI models downloaded to your Mac to run locally.
rules.regrows: Only if an app downloads the model again, which can take a while.
rules.safeToDelete: If you don't use this model anymore. You can download it again later.

patterns.title: Docker Desktop
patterns.guidance: Open Docker Desktop and use Troubleshoot › Clean / Purge data, or run “docker system prune -a” in Terminal.

patterns.title: OrbStack
patterns.guidance: In OrbStack, delete machines and images you no longer need, or run “docker system prune -a”.

patterns.title: Colima
patterns.guidance: Run “colima delete” for machines you no longer need.

patterns.title: Podman
patterns.guidance: Run “podman system prune” or remove unused machines with “podman machine rm”.

patterns.title: UTM virtual machines
patterns.guidance: Delete virtual machines you don't need from inside UTM.

patterns.title: Parallels virtual machines
patterns.guidance: Remove virtual machines you don't need in Parallels Desktop's Control Center.

rules.what: Disk images for virtual machines or containers. They often keep growing on their own.
rules.regrows: Yes, as you use the app that created them.
rules.safeToDelete: Not by deleting the file, which would lose everything inside. Clean up from the app itself.

action.guidance: Clean this up from inside the app that created it.

rules.what: Web content an app saved so it opens faster. Apps like Slack, Discord and VS Code are built this way.
rules.regrows: Yes. The app saves fresh copies as you use it.
rules.safeToDelete: Yes, while the app is closed.

rules.what: Records apps keep about what they did, including crash reports.
rules.regrows: Yes. Apps keep writing new logs as you use them.
rules.safeToDelete: Yes. You'd only need them to send to a developer about a problem.

rules.what: Temporary files Apple's own apps and services keep so things load faster.
rules.regrows: Yes. macOS rebuilds them as needed.
rules.safeToDelete: Usually. Some features may feel slower or sync again once.

rules.what: Temporary files apps keep so things load faster.
rules.regrows: Yes. Apps rebuild them as you use them, so the first launch may be a little slower.
rules.safeToDelete: Yes, while the app is closed.
